replyPlaybook.rule: There is no assumption named 'replyEarlyWindow' in x-2026-05-15.json — it does not exist in the profile and must not be cited as a real mechanism. The closest grounded guidance is: replyBoost (high confidence) — questions and direct conversation invitations meaningfully raise P(reply), a high-weight positive signal — and authorDiversityAttenuation (high confidence) — cadence matters more than volume within a session. The safe, grounded version of a 'reply window' rule is to spread the 10 daily replies across the day rather than bursting them, and to prioritize posts that are already inviting conversation, not to chase an unverified early-minutes velocity multiplier.
howToPick: Stay inside the proven veins (japanese-asian-design, retro-analog-preinternet, motion-animation-web, editorial-typography, music-hardware) rather than general tech/crypto/politics.

Prioritize accounts with a real audience — the quoteTargets list, or comparable reach — mirroring the measured gap between quoting low-reach accounts (~96 views) and higher-reach ones (11,451 views on the model's account).
Prioritize posts that are already asking a question or inviting discussion, per replyBoost.
Prioritize posts with visible native media (video/image) already attached, since a craft-specific reply needs something concrete to react to.

Skip posts showing hard-sell or engagement-bait language ('like if', 'buy now', 'limited time') per hardSellPenalty and engagementBaitPenalty — replying there risks association with content those assumptions predict gets suppressed.
Rotate targets so no single account gets replied to twice in the same day, keeping the reply activity itself topically and author-wise diverse.
replyShapes: Craft-specific technical reply: 'the easing on that hover state — spring or cubic-bezier? it doesn't overshoot the way most spring configs do.'
Build-along proof reply: 'rebuilt this exact grain effect in TSL last week, this is way cleaner than mine.'
One-line agreement + addition, no media: 'this is the actual argument against flat design and nobody says it this directly.'
Question-forward reply to invite a thread back: 'how's this holding up on lower-end GPUs? curious if the shader degrades gracefully.'
antipatterns: Replying with just an emoji or 'this is fire' — no craft content, doesn't function as an authority or reply-loop signal.
Replying to accounts with near-zero followings or engagement — the same low-reach problem measured in his quote-tweets.
Dropping a link in the reply — triggers the same linkRisk hypothesis as a primary post.
Replying across unrelated topics (politics, crypto, design) in the same day — works against topicConsistency instead of reinforcing a vein.
